analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה (‘his work that he had done’) is the direct object. The following וַיִּשְׁבֹּת (‘and he ceased’) confirms that God brought the work to completion.
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and an apocopated stem.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיְכַל (“he finished”) and וַיִּשְׁבֹּת (“he rested”), both third-person masculine singular verbs. The masculine singular suffix in מְלַאכְתּוֹ (“his work”) refers to the same divine actor.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular verb agreement.

analysis.evidence: The ordinal הַשְּׁבִיעִי ‘seventh’ modifies בַּיּוֹם. Together they identify the numbered day on which God finished his work.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed בְּ ‘on’ and the definite article.

analysis.evidence: In בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי, the adjective agrees with יוֹם in gender, number, and definiteness. It identifies the day on which God finished his work as the seventh.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute ordinal adjective.

analysis.evidence: מְלַאכְתּוֹ is the direct object of וַיְכַל, “he finished.” The suffix refers to אֱלֹהִים, and אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, “which he had done,” identifies the work as God’s activity of creation.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: In מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה (“his work which he had done”), אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying מְלַאכְתּוֹ. The work is the understood object of עָשָׂה.
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, “his work that he had done,” God is the subject of עָשָׂה, and “his work” supplies its object. The main verb וַיְכַל says that God finished that work.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ identifies what he ceased from: all his work. The preceding clause says he had finished that work.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּשְׁבֹּת בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי ‘he ceased on the seventh day’, the ordinal הַשְּׁבִיעִי identifies the day by its place in the sequence.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, prefixed with בְּ ‘on’ and the definite article הַ, together realized as בַּיּ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּשְׁבֹּת בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי, the ordinal agrees with יוֹם in gender, number, and definiteness. It identifies the seventh day as the day when God ceased from his work.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute ordinal adjective.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּשְׁבֹּת … מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, the prefix מִן marks what God ceased from, and כָּל takes מְלַאכְתּוֹ as its complement, referring to all the work he had done.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed מִן, whose נ assimilates to כ.

analysis.evidence: The marked מְלַאכְתּוֹ repeats the noun used earlier for the work God completed. With מִכָּל before it and אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה after it, the phrase identifies what God ceased from: “all his work that he had done.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular noun in the construct state with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ, referring to God.

analysis.evidence: In מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, “from all his work that he had done,” אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying מְלַאכְתּוֹ. The work is the understood object of עָשָׂה.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה, “from all his work that he had done,” God is the subject of עָשָׂה, and מְלַאכְתּוֹ supplies its object through the relative clause. The same wording occurs earlier in the verse at positions 4–6.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular
